definitions.explanation: A speech sound produced with vibration of the vocal cords. In Japanese, the voiced consonants include the g, z, d, b, and n series, typically marked with the dakuten (゛) diacritic.

examples.japanese: 「⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{有声音|ゆうせいおん}だ。
⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{濁点|だくてん}→濁点：27818_dakuten⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{有声音|ゆうせいおん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{示|しめ}す→示す：01948_shimesu⟧。
examples.english: In Japanese, the dakuten mark indicates a voiced sound.

examples.japanese: {有声音|ゆうせいおん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{無声音|むせいおん}→無声音：26421_museion⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{区別|くべつ}→区別：01555_kubetsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{外国語|がいこくご}→外国語：03023_gaikokugo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{発音|はつおん}→発音：01698_hatsuon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}ぶ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧とき⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{重要|じゅうよう}→重要：01575_juuyou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The distinction between voiced and voiceless sounds becomes important when learning foreign language pronunciation.

notes:
A compound of {有声|ゆうせい} (voiced, having voice) and {音|おん} (sound). In phonetics, voiced sounds are produced when the vocal cords vibrate during articulation.

JAPANESE VOICED CONSONANT SERIES:
- {が行|がぎょう} (ga, gi, gu, ge, go): voiced velar
- {ざ行|ざぎょう} (za, ji, zu, ze, zo): voiced alveolar
- {だ行|だぎょう} (da, ji, zu, de, do): voiced dental
- {ば行|ばぎょう} (ba, bi, bu, be, bo): voiced bilabial

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {有声音|ゆうせいおん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{無声音|むせいおん}→無声音：26421_museion⟧: voiced and voiceless sounds
- {有声音|ゆうせいおん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{変|か}わる→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧: to become voiced (voicing)
- {有声音|ゆうせいおん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{発音|はつおん}→発音：01698_hatsuon⟧: pronunciation of voiced sounds

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{無声音|むせいおん}→無声音：26421_museion⟧: voiceless sound — the opposite; produced without vocal cord vibration
- ⟦{濁音|だくおん}→濁音：19295_dakuon⟧: voiced kana — the kana-specific term for sounds marked with dakuten
- ⟦{清音|せいおん}→清音：23458_seion⟧: voiceless kana — the kana-specific term for basic unmarked sounds
